update.title: Made Work Report Git tracking package-aware
update.summary: Work Report now uses the report’s project identity as the repository context for commit metadata, diff statistics, and captured Git evidence, routing VCSH-backed packages through their independent histories.

blocks.body:
## Use the report’s project as repository context

Work Report now carries the project named on a report into every Git lookup. When that project maps to a VCSH repository, Git runs through `vcsh <project>`; conventional repositories continue through Git directly.

This connects reporting to Constellation’s package ownership structure, so the report selects the repository responsible for the work instead of treating the shared filesystem as one Git boundary.

blocks.caption: The report’s project identity selects one repository route for every Git fact and stored piece of evidence.
blocks.code:
flowchart LR
  Report[Report project identity] --> Route{Repository adapter}
  Route -->|Standard repository| Git[Direct Git]
  Route -->|VCSH package| VCSH[Package VCSH repository]
  Git & VCSH --> Facts[Commit + diff facts]
  Facts --> Evidence[Stored report evidence]
blocks.summary: The report’s project identity selects one repository route for every Git fact and stored piece of evidence.

blocks.body:
## Keep every recorded Git fact on the same route

The statistics collector and Git evidence handler now use the same repository context for commit lookup, file changes, diff text, and commit messages. The numerical summary and retained evidence therefore come from the same package history.

part_of.title: Built Work Report System to preserve completed work
part_of.summary: Created a command-line reporting tool that records what changed, why it changed, project context, commit statistics, and file or image references as searchable PostgreSQL records.

related.title: Separated package histories with VCSH
related.summary: Constellation now uses VCSH to track packages independently inside one shared workspace, giving every package a formal Git ownership boundary without splitting apart the files that work together.
